answer: The strongest lever is simple: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because kernel only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. In practice trellis is enforced by the ledger itself: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any pigment approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
